title: Group Security Inventory filter token configs under a tokens/ folder
description:
<!--IssueSummary start-->

<details>
<summary>

Everyone can contribute. [Help move this issue forward](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/marketing/developer-relations/contributor-success/community-contributors-workflows/#contributor-links) while earning points, leveling up and collecting rewards.

</summary>

- [Label this issue](https://contributors.gitlab.com/manage-issue?action=label&projectId=278964&issueIid=607770)

</details>

<!--IssueSummary end-->

## Problem

Three filter token configuration files sit as siblings of Vue components in `ee/app/assets/javascripts/security_inventory/components/`:

- `tool_coverage_tokens.js`
- `vulnerability_count_tokens.js`
- `status_tokens.js` (added in gitlab-org/gitlab#607768)

These are not Vue components. They are static configuration objects that describe search-bar tokens. Grouping them under a dedicated `tokens/` subfolder gives them a clear home, keeps the `components/` directory focused on Vue files, and makes it obvious where to add the next token config.

## Proposal

Move the three files to `ee/app/assets/javascripts/security_inventory/components/tokens/`:

- `tool_coverage_tokens.js` -> `tokens/tool_coverage_tokens.js`
- `vulnerability_count_tokens.js` -> `tokens/vulnerability_count_tokens.js`
- `status_tokens.js` -> `tokens/status_tokens.js`

Update the two importers to point at the new paths:

- `ee/app/assets/javascripts/security_inventory/components/inventory_dashboard_filtered_search_bar.vue`
- `ee/spec/frontend/security_inventory/components/inventory_dashboard_filtered_search_bar_spec.js`

## Scope

Pure move plus import path updates. No behavior change, no logic change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The three token config files live under `components/tokens/`
- [ ] Both importers reference the new paths
- [ ] `yarn jest ee/spec/frontend/security_inventory/components/inventory_dashboard_filtered_search_bar_spec.js` passes
- [ ] No other files reference the old paths

## Out of scope

- Any change to token behavior, options, or operators
- Any change to the search bar component itself

title: Add project status filter to Security Inventory search bar
description:
<!--IssueSummary start-->

<details>
<summary>

Everyone can contribute. [Help move this issue forward](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/marketing/developer-relations/contributor-success/community-contributors-workflows/#contributor-links) while earning points, leveling up and collecting rewards.

</summary>

- [Label this issue](https://contributors.gitlab.com/manage-issue?action=label&projectId=278964&issueIid=607768)

</details>

<!--IssueSummary end-->

## Problem

The group Security Configuration page has 4 status cards ("Needs attention", "Stale scans", "Unprotected projects", "Scanners enabled"). Each card's "View projects" action opens a modal filtered to projects in that status, backed by `namespaceSecurityProjects` with the `hasFailedOrWarning`, `hasStale`, and `hasScanners` arguments.

The Security Inventory page shows the same projects but its filtered search bar cannot filter by these three aggregate statuses. A user who clicks through from a configuration card sees the filtered list in a modal but loses the filter as soon as they navigate to the inventory to inspect a project in context.

## Proposal

Add a new **Status** token to the Security Inventory filtered search bar with three single-select options:

- `Needs attention` (maps to `hasFailedOrWarning: true`)
- `Stale scans` (maps to `hasStale: true`)
- `Unprotected projects` (maps to `hasScanners: false`)

Labels match the Security Configuration card labels exactly so users moving between the two surfaces see consistent wording.

The token uses `OPERATORS_IS` (equal) and `unique: true`, so only one Status filter is active at a time. Switching values reuses the same token, matching the **work item** Status pattern. The token renders at the top of the dropdown as an independent entry above the **Security attributes** section, not nested under any bold section header.

## Scope

Frontend only. The arguments `hasScanners`, `hasFailedOrWarning`, and `hasStale` already exist on the `namespaceSecurityProjects` resolver (see `ee/app/graphql/resolvers/security/namespace_security_projects_resolver.rb`, experiment-flagged for milestone 19.0). No backend, database, or GraphQL schema changes are needed.

### Changes

1. Add `$hasScanners`, `$hasFailedOrWarning`, `$hasStale` variables to `ee/app/assets/javascripts/security_inventory/graphql/namespace_security_projects.query.graphql` and pass them to the `namespaceSecurityProjects` field.
2. Add a `status_tokens.js` config alongside the existing `tool_coverage_tokens.js` and `vulnerability_count_tokens.js`, and register it in `inventory_dashboard_filtered_search_bar.vue`.
3. Wire the token into `inventory_dashboard.vue` so its value maps to the three boolean variables in every Apollo query call, and extend `hasSearch` so the search query fires when a Status is set.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A **Status** token appears in the Security Inventory search bar
- [x] The token offers three options: `Needs attention`, `Stale scans`, `Unprotected projects`
- [x] Selecting an option filters the project list to match
- [x] Only one Status filter is active at a time
- [x] The Status token renders as an independent entry at the top of the dropdown, above the **Security attributes** section, with no bold section header of its own
- [x] Clearing the token restores the unfiltered list
- [x] Frontend specs cover the token config and the query mapping

## Out of scope

- Backend changes: none needed
- URL persistence for the Status filter: existing filter tokens do not URL-sync, and doing it for Status alone would be inconsistent. If wanted, a separate issue should cover all tokens uniformly.
- Cross-linking from the configuration cards into a pre-filtered inventory view (nice future improvement, tracked separately)

## Related

- MR: gitlab-org/gitlab!248223
- Follow-up refactor to group filter token configs under `components/tokens/`: gitlab-org/gitlab#607770

title: Fork source branch is unreadable in MR header due to truncation
description:
### Summary

![fork-mr](/uploads/3116e8bcb841a1606175d0cdca3b682c/fork-mr.png){width=900 height=111}

The MR page header reads "[username] requested to merge [source] into [target]".
When the MR comes from a fork, the source branch is rendered as `namespace/project:branch`
(e.g. `gitlab-community/gitlab-org/gitlab:skkzsh/markup-path-cache-key`),
which is much longer than a plain branch name.

On fork MRs, most of this label ends up truncated to `…`,
so you can't tell at a glance which project and branch the MR comes from.
Worse, every MR from the same fork shows the exact same label
(e.g. `gitlab-community/gitlab-org/git…` for all MRs from the Community fork),
so the header effectively carries no information.

### Examples

```glql
# display: table
# fields: title
title: "fork MRs"
# sort: dueDate asc
limit: 2
query: type = MergeRequest and state = opened and label = ~"Community contribution" and project = "gitlab-org/gitlab"
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open any MR submitted from the
   [GitLab Community fork](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-community/gitlab)
   to upstream
1. Look at the header below the MR title

### What is the current *bug* behavior?

The source branch label is cut off partway through the fork's project path,
e.g. `gitlab-community/gitlab-org/git…`,
so neither the project name nor the branch name is readable.

### What is the expected *correct* behavior?

The fork's project path and branch name are readable,
at least when there is enough horizontal space.
Failing that, truncation keeps the most useful part (the trailing branch name).

### Output of checks

This bug happens on GitLab.com


### Possible fixes

The source branch gets `gl-max-w-26` (`max-width: 13rem` ≈ 208px)
and `gl-truncate`, whether or not the MR comes from a fork.
The `namespace/project:branch` format on fork MRs easily exceeds the fixed 13rem.

A few possible directions:

- Let the label use the available horizontal space instead of a fixed width
- Truncate from the left so the trailing branch name stays visible
- Relax the `max-width` only for fork MRs

title: Work item status change trigger does not fire when status changes via issue close, only via the status widget
description:
## Summary

The Duo Agent Platform **Work item (Status changed)** trigger fires only when a work item's status is changed through the status widget. It does not fire when the same status change is produced by closing the issue — either from the issue's three-dots menu or by merging an MR that references `Closes #N`.

Both paths produce an identical resulting state and an identical `set status to **Complete**` system note. Only one of them starts a flow session.

The practical effect is that the trigger misses the most common way work items reach a terminal status in a normal workflow: being closed by a merged merge request.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Custom Flow in a project and configure a **Work item (Status changed)** trigger for it.
2. Create a test issue.
3. Close the issue using the **Close issue** action in the three-dots menu. In a project with the status widget enabled, this also sets status to **Complete** and writes a `set status to **Complete**` system note.
4. Reopen the issue.
5. Set status to **Complete** using the **status widget**. This also sets state to closed.

## Current behaviour

- **Step 3 (close via menu):** system note `set status to **Complete**` is written. **No flow session is started.** No trigger activity of any kind.
- **Step 5 (status widget):** system note `set status to **Complete**` is written, and the flow starts within ~1 second.

The same divergence occurs when an issue is closed by merging an MR containing `Closes #N` — status becomes Complete, no session starts.

Observed on GitLab.com (19.3.0) in a private project. Verified twice on the same issue, alternating between the two paths, with all other configuration held constant. The two system notes are indistinguishable in content and author.

## Expected behaviour

The trigger should fire whenever a work item's status value actually changes, regardless of which code path caused the change. A consumer subscribing to "status changed" reasonably expects the event to reflect the status having changed — not the specific UI affordance used to change it.

At minimum, closure-driven status transitions should emit the event, since closing an issue is a primary way status reaches a terminal value.

## Suspected cause

Issue #606553 ("Trigger generic AI event when work item status changes") describes the scope as:

> Emit a `work_item_status_changed` AI event **after a successful status widget update**, carrying the work item identity, previous status, new status, and the acting user.

If the emission is hooked to the status widget update path specifically, rather than to the underlying status attribute change, that would explain the observed behaviour precisely. State-driven status transitions (close → Complete) bypass the widget path and therefore emit nothing.

If that is the case, this may be better characterised as an incomplete implementation than a regression — but the trigger's user-facing name and description give no indication that it is scoped to a single mutation path, so it currently behaves as a bug from a consumer's perspective.

## Impact

For any automation that reacts to work completing, this makes the trigger close to unusable:

- Issues closed by a merged MR — the dominant completion path in a normal development workflow — never fire the trigger.
- Issues closed manually from the issue view never fire the trigger.
- Only a deliberate status-widget edit fires it, which is the case where a human is already in the work item and could invoke the flow directly.

The trigger therefore fires least often in exactly the unattended scenarios automation is meant to cover, and most often in the scenario that least needs it.

## Proposal

Emit `work_item_status_changed` on any successful change to the status value, including:

- Status set via the status widget (current behaviour).
- Status changed as a consequence of a state transition (close/reopen), whether initiated from the UI, the API, or a `Closes #N` reference in a merged commit or MR.

The event payload described in #606553 (work item identity, previous status, new status, acting user) appears sufficient for all of these; for commit-driven closures, the acting user would be the user whose merge caused the closure.

If emitting on all paths is not desirable, the trigger's name and description should state explicitly which mutation paths it covers, so that flow authors do not design around an event that will not arrive.

## Related

- #606553 — Trigger generic AI event when work item status changes (likely origin of the current scoping)
- &22883 — Status update triggers

title: Harden Ci::PipelineArtifact callers against a missing file
description:
## Summary

The pipeline variables artifact file can be missing from object storage.
This can happen when the file upload fails after the database record is
already committed. Callers of `Ci::PipelineArtifact` do not check if the
file exists. We must make these callers safe against a missing file.

## Background

MR !244224 removed a transaction wrapper around
`Ci::CreateDownstreamPipelineWorker`. The change reduced idle-in-transaction
time only a little. Most idle-in-transaction time comes from the
`INSERT INTO ci_pipeline_artifacts` query. See !244224#note_3536080515.

MR !244299 tried to fix this. The MR moved the pipeline variables artifact
file upload to an `after_commit` callback, behind a feature flag. This
removes the idle-in-transaction time. But the change has a risk: if the
upload fails after the database commit, the pipeline record has no file.
The MR destroys the pipeline in this case, but some side effects of
pipeline creation (keep-around refs, internal event tracking) cannot be
undone. This can leave inconsistent state.

We also found existing missing-file errors in Sentry
(https://new-sentry.gitlab.net/organizations/gitlab/issues/3875534). These
errors happen today, without the after-commit change. This confirms that
callers do not handle a missing file correctly, regardless of this MR.

Per !244299#note_3630476625: keep the `after_commit` approach, but harden
the callers first. Close !244299 in favor of this issue.

## Goal

Make all callers of `Ci::PipelineArtifact` (pipeline_variables file type)
safe against a missing file.

## Proposed work

1. Find all read paths for the pipeline_variables artifact (for example,
   `Ci::Pipeline#variables`).
2. Add a missing-file check to each read path. Return a safe, clear
   result. Do not return a server error to the user.
3. Find all write paths that depend on the artifact file.
4. Add a missing-file check to each write path. Fail the operation with a
   `data_integrity_failure` error. Do not continue with an empty file.
5. Add tests for the missing-file case in each hardened path.
6. Re-open the `after_commit` upload change from !244299 once the callers
   are hardened.

## References

- Original MR: !244224
- Follow-up MR (superseded by this issue): !244299
- Comment that started this issue: !244299#note_3630476625
- Idle-in-transaction data: !244224#note_3536080515
- Existing missing-file errors: https://new-sentry.gitlab.net/organizations/gitlab/issues/3875534
- Feature flag rollout issue: gitlab-org/gitlab#605240
